verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents its own programmatic surface: an official MCP server and service keys for 'AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace.' An OAuth-connected assistant 'can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows,' which implies role-bounded action but does not establish API-to-UI parity. No public API reference or OpenAPI spec was found (probes returned 404), so the breadth of coverage is unproven. Missing for 10: documented API reference/OpenAPI spec, explicit statement or evidence of full UI-to-API parity, per-feature endpoint coverage, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Use **service keys** for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows
Grant Full access to all tenant service-key scopes, or choose Limit access to… to grant only specific scopes.
